title: Sachems Who Played in College & Beyond
status: Research in progress; additions require verified college or professional football roster evidence. Saugus, Massachusetts, not Saugus, California.
eligibility: A documented college or professional roster spot qualifies even without game appearances; redshirts, reserves, and practice squads count. Being drafted or invited to a tryout does not alone establish a professional roster spot.

entries.name: Art Statuto
entries.notes: Reserve center on Notre Dame national championship teams; professional playing career documented.

entries.name: Doug Waybright
entries.professional: 1948 AAFC draft selection (Buffalo); professional roster not confirmed
entries.notes: Notre Dame’s historical lineups and 1949 Football Review document his Irish career; a draft selection alone is not counted as professional roster membership. Saugus Class of 1944 verified directly by his senior portrait and activities entry in the 1944 Tontoquonian yearbook (page 28), supplied by contributor; this primary source supersedes the conflicting 1945 retrospective.

entries.notes: Ohio State football, 1976–1979 (years supplied by Saugus contributor). Practice and offseason professional affiliations are included under the roster-only standard.

entries.name: Steve Gannon
entries.professional: Cincinnati Bengals (NFL free-agent signing; released); New York Giants (NFL signing; released during roster cuts)
entries.notes: All-New England defensive end at Holy Cross; 1975 Lynn Item All-Star at Saugus. Signed as an NFL free agent by Cincinnati, then signed with the Giants 12 days before his release, according to a contemporary newspaper clipping supplied by a contributor. Holy Cross Hall of Fame inductee (2020).

entries.name: John Nicolo
entries.notes: Four-year letterwinner; captain and All-American on Ithaca’s 1979 NCAA Division III championship team.

entries.name: Steve Peach
entries.notes: Syracuse: 1981 redshirt (contributor-reported); 1982 QB, 26 completions on 65 attempts for 372 yards and 1 passing TD. Boston College: 1983 transfer redshirt (contributor-reported); 1984 punter, 46 punts for 1,678 yards (36.5 average); 1985 QB/punter, 72 punts for 2,591 yards (36.0 average), 14-of-31 passing for 297 yards and 1 TD. BC totals: 118 punts, 4,269 yards, 36.2 average. Redshirt seasons not independently verified.

entries.name: L.J. McKanas
entries.notes: Northeastern Hall of Fame inductee; redshirt season included under roster-based eligibility.

entries.name: Mike Nicolo
entries.rosterYears: 2005–2008 (2005–2007 game participation documented; 2008 pending separate verification)
entries.notes: Played at Curry College from 2005 through 2008 (years supplied by contributor). Curry's official 2007 cumulative statistics confirm No. 14 Michael Nicolo appeared in 12 games, recording 13 solo tackles and 6 assisted tackles (19 total) on Curry's 12–1 team. He also logged one rushing attempt for −10 yards. Game participation also documented in 2005 and 2006; 2008 season evidence remains to be located.

entries.name: Raphael Zammit
entries.notes: Curry running back, 2000–2003. Career: 800 carries, 4,353 rushing yards, 44 rushing TDs; 46 kickoff returns for 1,131 yards and 2 punt-return TDs. 2002: 1,479 rushing yards, 18 rushing TDs; 2003: 1,587 rushing yards, 12 rushing TDs. First Team All-Conference (2002, 2003); Second Team All-Conference (2000, 2001); Conference Offensive Player of the Year (2002, 2003); National Third Team All-American (2002, 2003); ECAC All-Region First Team (2002, 2003); NEFWA Division II/III All-Star (2002, 2003); NEFWA Gold Helmet weekly award (2002, 2003). Source: Curry College Football Record Book, updated January 2025.
